reviewed_by: Claude general-purpose subagent, blind judgment reviewer, round-5 fix-verification batch

samples_reviewed.question_text: In 135, what digit is in the ones place?
What place is the digit 1 in, in the number 195?
What is the place value of the digit 3 in 320?
What is the place value of the digit 8 in 285?
In 230, what digit is in the ones place?

competency_fulfillment.rationale: I hand-verified every one of the 8 answers: digit 1 in 195 is hundreds (43), digit 3 in 320 has place value 300 (44), digit 8 in 285 has place value 80 (45), digit 0 in 260 is ones (46), digit 5 in 250 is tens (49); all check out for a 3-digit number.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: Unlike the stale prior review (which flagged the reverse-lookup clause as entirely untested), this batch now includes seeds 42 and 48 ('In 135/230, what digit is in the ones place?'), genuinely exercising all three sub-skills named in the competency across the 8 seeds.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: The repeated frames ('In N, what digit is in the ones place?', 'What place is the digit D in, in the number N?') are concise and appropriate for grade-2 quarter-1 students newly introduced to 3-digit numbers and the hundreds place.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Across the 8 seeds the answers span all three positions (hundreds via 43, tens via 47/49, ones via 42/46/48) and both directions (name-the-place and identify-the-digit), a meaningfully fuller variant space than the prior stale review found.

competency_alignment.rationale: All numbers used (135-320) are genuine 3-digit values that correctly exercise the newly-introduced hundreds place, matching the grade-2 scope of this lc rather than the 2-digit grade-1 or 4-digit grade-3 siblings.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: 3-digit numbers (135 to 320) with place values up to 300 are appropriately scaled to grade-2 quarter-1 place-value expectations, matching the newly-introduced 'hundreds' vocabulary for this node.
